articles.title: Australia v England: Sam Curran strikes with 'moon ball' - what makes it effective?
articles.summary: Statistics show Sam Curran's 'moon ball' is one of his most effective weapons. How does he do it and what makes it so effective?
articles.body:
The 'moon ball' worked again for Sam Curran in Adelaide on Sunday.

The England all-rounder has had a tricky run since he returned from injury last month, taking only four wickets at an average of 55.75 in five one-day internationals before boarding the flight from Perth.

But Curran was rewarded for returning to his tried and tested in the second ODI against Australia.

With the first ball of a new spell Curran bowled Jack Edwards with that trademark slower ball - this one clocked slower than many spinners at 50mph.

Edwards, head rocking back and arm on his hip, looked like a man frustrated to have been deceived.

He is not the first to be done by Curran's moon ball. It is one of the 28-year-old's most potent weapons.

Data from analysts CricViz suggests he is averaging 17 with deliveries under 90km/h (56mph) in ODIs since the start of 2025, when he developed the delivery. When bowling above 90km/h, he averages 45.16.

The dismissal of Edwards was his fourth moon-ball wicket. India pair Shreyas Iyer and Ishan Kishan and Sri Lanka's Pathum Nissanka have fallen for the trap in the 50-over format.

Curran was clocked bowling as low as 43mph earlier this year. His top speeds - about 83mph - may be modest, but it is the difference, and the deception, that is effective.

Speaking on the For the Love of Cricket podcast this year, Curran said: "You have to be creative. Guys are developing so fast.

"I've worked so hard on trying to keep the arm speed the same and then I've got better at landing the ball at the right length."

The length of the Edwards dismissal - about 2m from the stumps and by the right-hander's toes - was the fullest of all of his moon-ball wickets.

They have all come from deliveries pitched 6m or fuller. Go shorter and the delivery is not as effective.

With the growth of T20 leagues and batters hitting harder and further, bowlers are having to develop new techniques and an effective slower ball to combat them.

Former England pace bowler Steve Harmison, who famously bamboozled Michael Clarke with a 65mph yorker in the 2005 Ashes, said Curran's ability to disguise the delivery is key to its success.

"You can see his release point is a lot further back than [his off-cutter]," he said on TNT Sports.

"With the moon ball, he is just hoping that the batter gets lost in his movement and body shape.

"He holds the ball between his first finger and his thumb, throws the ball in the air and tries to keep the same arm speed, but the ball comes out behind him much slower."

Ironically, it is the lack of speed that kills.

The delivery that fooled Nissanka was slower than all of spinner Rehan Ahmed's previous six balls in the innings during an ODI this year.

"It does get hit, but I feel if a batter knows I can do something a little bit unique, like when you face a mystery spinner, they might have a bit more doubt," said Curran.

Former England fast bowler Tymal Mills, who has played against Curran in The Hundred and the T20 Blast, said the variation is difficult to pick.

"I faced Sam in The Hundred and it's hard to hit," he said.

"You've got to wait for the ball so long. You're expecting the ball to come to you and it's just kind of floating out there.

"The more you bowl it, the more guys will cotton on to it. I'm sure he'll adapt again."

Why have fast bowlers developed a stock slow ball?

Mills has clocked speeds up to 93mph, but says having a slow ball is crucial for any bowler.

"You need to be evolving, you need to be adapting and you need to be trying to add a new skill because the game changes all the time," he said.

"It goes in cycles and you need to keep going into different tricks that you've got at various different times."

Former England seamer Jade Dernbach, who developed a go-to back-of-the-hand slower ball to much success, agrees.

"You have to have that sort of variety nowadays, the way one-day cricket is going," he said.

"You can't just be a one-trick pony any more. The game is developing so quickly that you have to develop with it on a yearly basis."

With bowlers like Curran continuing to find new ways to innovate, the moon ball is just one more thing for batters to be worried about.

articles.title: IND vs NZ: After sitting out four games, Mohammed Siraj gets his chance in fifth ODI; Yash Thakur makes debut
articles.summary: Mohammed Siraj finally got an opportunity in the series as India brought back the experienced pacer for the fifth and final ODI against New Zealand at Bay
articles.body: Mohammed Siraj finally got an opportunity in the series as India brought back the experienced pacer for the fifth and final ODI against New Zealand at Bay Oval in Mount Maunganui on Sunday. It is Siraj's first appearance in the series. He last played an ODI against the West Indies in October."Siraj has been craving an opportunity to play in all formats. He's been around the team for a while and is pretty experienced. He's played over the years, so he knows how to go about things. We're super excited for him as well," India captain Shreyas Iyer said at the toss.New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner won the toss and elected to bowl in the series-deciding match. India lead the five-match series 2-1 after winning the first two games, while the third ODI was washed out. The visitors, however, suffered a 244-run defeat in the fourth match on Friday.India also handed a debut to right-arm seamer Yash Thakur. "He's a jovial guy who has been waiting for the opportunity to play for the country and has been in the scheme of things for a while. I'm glad he's getting the opportunity to prove himself today. It's his debut, so good luck to him," Iyer said.India's Gurnoor Brar and New Zealand's Matt Henry and Kyle Jamieson will miss the final ODI as they prepare for the two-Test series, which begins on November 19.Teams:India: Rohit Sharma, Ruturaj Gaikwad, Virat Kohli, Shreyas Iyer (c), Ishan Kishan (wk), Axar Patel, Naman Dhir, Auqib Nabi, Arshdeep Singh, Mohammed Siraj, Yash Thakur.New Zealand: Tim Seifert (wk), Will Young, Nick Kelly, Dean Foxcroft, Finn Allen, Michael Bracewell, Mitchell Santner (c), Kristian Clarke, Blair Tickner, Jacob Duffy, Matthew FisherGet the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Aaryavir, a Rishabh Pant fan, learnt to refrain from copying father Sehwag
articles.summary: When Virender Sehwag dropped his 11-year-old son Aaryavir at the Sonnet Cricket Club eight years ago, he made just one request to the coaches, the late
articles.body: When Virender Sehwag dropped his 11-year-old son Aaryavir at the Sonnet Cricket Club eight years ago, he made just one request to the coaches, the late Tarak Sinha and Devender Sharma. “Don’t hesitate to be strict with him. He is just another kid learning cricket here. That's all he told us,” Devender told TOI.“Viru barely called us to enquire about how his sons were coached. He must have talked to them personally but never interfered in our job. The only time he made a call about Aaryavir’s cricket was during the Covid lockdown. He shot some videos of some of his batting drills and sent them to us to check,” he added.Aaryavir was given a swanky car to come to the ground, but the chauffer was strictly instructed against carrying his kit bags. Be it the cricket gear or the food he ate there, nothing was special. His demeanour didn’t give him away as the son of one of India’s greatest match-winners.Now, over the last 10 days in Al Amerat in Oman, Aaryavir has taken significant steps towards developing his own identity. His ended as the player of the tournament, scoring 361 runs.Like his father did in his first big final against England at Lord’s in 2002, Aaryavir set up India’s big chase at the top of the order on Saturday with 58 off 61 balls. “Since I got out in the last match against them (Pakistan), I wanted to score today, regardless of copping a blow on my arm. I knew if I stayed in the middle, it would keep building the pressure on Pakistan,” Aaryavir words after the final were reminiscent of Sehwag's unfettered ways.It’s worth noticing that Aaryavir’s runs have not come in the same menacing way that the senior Sehwag was known for. “He has learnt to refrain from copying Viru,” Devender, who has played U-19 and first-class cricket with Sehwag, told TOI. Instead, Aaryavir used to be in awe of Rishabh Pant. “He used to go home and keep talking about Rishabh. Whenever Rishabh came for practice, he would intently watch him,” Devender said."There is some obvious reflection of Viru's talent in him. One must understand Viru was a freak and a beast. But Aaryavir is a very cerebral cricketer. When he first came, he compulsively tried to smack every ball off the front foot because he may have seen highlights of his father's batting," said Devender. "But, he likes to have deep discussions on cricket and tried to understand why he was getting out quickly. He realised the importance of being a good off the back foot and playing square of the wicket just like his father did. I am pleased that he scored a 160 in this tournament because he has been working hard on cracking the code to construct big innings," he added.Devender emphasizes on Viru's lack of interference in how both his sons are raised in the cricket field and helped them develop their individuality. Sehwag's uncluttered mind helped him revel as a player. Aaryavir may have done his bit in shedding some of the burden of carrying his father's name. It's time to build on it!Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Virat Kohli, Rohit Sharma miss the beat in their last dance on New Zealand soil
articles.summary: MIUNT MANGANUI: The coastal city of Tauranga broke away from the wet script witnessed in Auckland, Wellington and Hamilton, but even the bright sunshine
articles.body: MIUNT MANGANUI: The coastal city of Tauranga broke away from the wet script witnessed in Auckland, Wellington and Hamilton, but even the bright sunshine couldn't change the narrative for Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli in New Zealand. The experienced campaigners managed series hauls of just 86 and 30 runs, respectively, in conditions that remained challenging for batters.The ODI specialists would have liked better returns, but their last dance in New Zealand never found the right beat. Kohli did score an authoritative 74 in the series opener at Eden Park but lost rhythm after that. His last three scores were 7, 0 and 5. For Rohit, it was a difficult tour, with two ducks, and he crossed the double-digit mark only once. On only their second overseas tour of the year, the two right-handers struggled against pace, bounce, movement and the sheer relentlessness of the Kiwi quicks.Their vulnerabilities against the moving ball were exposed as the opposition didn't give an inch, persisting with the good-length spot and coupling it with movement in either direction. Both were caught on the crease in the fourth ODI and lacked confidence in the final fixture. Rohit mistimed a flick, while Kohli slashed at a delivery outside off, leaving India in trouble in both fixtures even before the spectators could settle down.While Matt Henry operated in unplayable territory on Friday, Sunday afternoon was a perfect occasion to cash in. More than movement off the pitch or in the air, it was their shot selection that kept the two batters' series hauls low. Overall, 2026 has been a rewarding year for the two, but New Zealand has been an opposition against which Rohit hasn't enjoyed any success, both at home and away. As far as Kohli is concerned, it was a rare failure after what has been a very high-scoring year for India's No. 3.Misfiring top orderIndia's top order misfired throughout the series, and this was the first occasion in over five years when none of the top three scored an individual hundred. It has happened only twice since the 2013 Champions Trophy that India's top order failed to reach the three-figure mark in a five-match series. Interestingly, both instances came against the same opposition: New Zealand, in 2019 and now during this tour.This away vulnerability will definitely serve as a stern wake-up call in the build-up to the 2027 ODI World Cup, where head coach Gautam Gambhir expects similar conditions. India will again find home comfort against Sri Lanka and Zimbabwe after this tour, but doubts over whether the batting has what it takes to dominate in South Africa will continue.For the first time in over 10 years, Kohli registered three single-digit scores in an ODI series, while the two ducks saw Rohit join several unwanted lists. There are no doubts about their abilities in the format, but it now remains to be seen how the think tank reviews these struggles as it firms up its plans for next year's multi-nation event.India will need experience in South Africa, but more than that, they will need two firing and assured batters in the top three.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Virat Kohli hits 11-year low as India suffer another batting collapse in New Zealand
articles.summary: Virat Kohli endured a difficult ODI series against New Zealand, managing just 86 runs in four innings as India suffered another batting collapse in the
articles.body: Virat Kohli endured a difficult ODI series against New Zealand, managing just 86 runs in four innings as India suffered another batting collapse in the fifth and final match in Mount Maunganui on Sunday. The 38-year-old had arrived in New Zealand after scoring runs in India's previous ODI series against the West Indies, but could not carry that form into the contest against the Black Caps.Kohli, who holds the record for the most ODI runs against New Zealand, started the series with a 74 off 51 balls in the opening match at Eden Park in Auckland on November 4. However, his scores in the next three innings were 7, 0 and 5, respectively.The three single-digit scores in the second, fourth and fifth ODIs marked a first for Kohli in 11 years. The right-handed batter had last recorded three single-digit scores in an ODI series in 2015.Since making his ODI debut against Sri Lanka in Dambulla on August 18, 2008, Kohli had previously registered three single-digit scores in a bilateral series against Pakistan during their tour of India in December 2012-January 2013. He scored 0, 6 and 7 in the matches played in Chennai, Kolkata and Delhi, respectively.Kohli has also had two other ODI tournaments in which he recorded three single-digit scores. These came during the 2011 World Cup and the Carlton Mid ODI Tri-Series in Australia in 2014-15.Kohli's three single-digit scores in an ODI series or tournament:- 2011 World Cup- Pakistan in India, 2012-13- Carlton Mid ODI Tri-Series, Australia, 2014-15- India vs New Zealand, 2026India's batting struggles continued in the fifth ODI, with New Zealand bowling out the visitors for 209 in the series decider in Mount Maunganui on Sunday. The hosts' bowlers maintained their lines and troubled the Indian batters, putting themselves in a position to level the series.The Shreyas Iyer-led side had been expected to put up a better performance after being bowled out for 89 at the same venue in the fourth ODI a couple of days earlier. articles.title: Arshdeep Singh equals two batting records with quickfire knock in fifth ODI
articles.summary: Arshdeep Singh made the most of his brief stay at the crease after walking out to bat at No.
articles.body: Arshdeep Singh made the most of his brief stay at the crease after walking out to bat at No. 11 for India in the fifth and final ODI against New Zealand on Sunday. The left-arm pacer scored 14 runs off just four balls, hitting two sixes before being dismissed by Jacob Duffy in the 43rd over.Arshdeep opened his account with a six off the first ball he faced, sending Duffy over the boundary. He hit another six off the third delivery before Duffy dismissed him on the first ball of the 43rd over.The two sixes helped Arshdeep match two batting records for India in ODIs. By hitting a six off the first ball of his innings, he became only the third Indian No. 11 batter to achieve the feat.Before Arshdeep, Venkatesh Prasad and Jasprit Bumrah had also hit sixes off the first ball of their innings while batting at No. 11 for India.Prasad achieved the feat against Australia in the quarter-final of the 2000 Champions Trophy, then known as the ICC Knockout Trophy, in Nairobi. Bumrah hit Pat Cummins for a six off the first ball of his innings in an ODI against Australia in Mohali on March 10, 2019.India No. 11 batters to hit a six off the first ball of their innings in an ODI:- Venkatesh Prasad off Ian Harvey (Australia), Nairobi, 2000 Champions Trophy quarter-final- Jasprit Bumrah off Pat Cummins (Australia), Mohali, 2019- Arshdeep Singh off Jacob Duffy (New Zealand), Mount Maunganui, 2026Where data is availableArshdeep's two sixes also helped him equal the record for the most sixes by an Indian No. 11 batter in an ODI innings. articles.body: Former Australia fast bowler Chadd Sayers has challenged Pat Cummins’ version of the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, backing Usman Khawaja’s claim that the entire Australian team knew about the plan to use sandpaper during the South Africa tour.Sayers, who was part of the touring squad, said he believed every player was aware of what was happening. He also disagreed with Cummins’ statement that there was no team discussion about taking collective responsibility after the incident.“I’m comfortable sitting here … that I believe that everyone in that side knew what was going on and what was being used,” Sayers told SEN radio on Sunday. “I’m not taking sides. I’m neutral in all this, I’m just trying to tell my side of the story and what I believe happened.”The controversy has returned to the spotlight following Khawaja’s autobiography, in which he claimed the entire team knew about the sandpaper plan and suggested Australia had used ball-tampering methods even before the Cape Town Test in 2018.Cummins dismissed Khawaja’s allegations as “complete nonsense” during a press conference on Friday. However, Sayers was unhappy with how the Australian captain addressed the issue, particularly his personal comments about Khawaja.“I didn’t like how he [Cummins] did go at Usman and got personal. I probably get why but I don’t think it needed to happen.”Sayers recalls team meeting after scandalSayers also remembered a lengthy discussion among players after the incident came to light. This contradicts Cummins’ version of events.“We all sat in the change rooms after that day’s play, probably for 60 to 90 minutes, and just talked about what had happened and where to next,” Sayers said.He added that he was relieved the matter was finally being discussed openly after years of players having to remain silent.Warner questions Cricket Australia's investigationMeanwhile, former vice-captain David Warner has again questioned Cricket Australia’s investigation, alleging that important information was withheld from him. Warner, along with Steve Smith and Cameron Bancroft, was punished following the scandal.Warner claimed he was never informed that bowlers had been interviewed during the investigation and questioned why the governing body had not shared all the evidence with him before he accepted his punishment.“Just to clarify ‘As far as I am aware’ was the POINT,” he wrote on Instagram. “I was never told the bowlers had been interviewed or provided statements.“That information would’ve been pretty useful when I was forced to make decisions back in 2018. articles.title: Sandpaper scandal: Bowler Chadd Sayers says he took sandpaper from the field and rejects Pat Cummins recount
articles.summary: Australia bowler Chadd Sayers says he helped take sandpaper from the field in the match prior to the Cape Town Test and backs Usman Khawaja's recollection over Pat Cummins'.
articles.body:
Former Australia bowler Chadd Sayers says he helped take sandpaper off the ground in the match before the infamous Cape Town Test and has backed Usman Khawaja's recollection over Pat Cummins' - saying he believes "everyone knew" about the plan to ball tamper.

Sayers, 39, was 12th man during the second Test of the 2018 series against South Africa in Gqeberha, previously known as Port Elizabeth, and backed the claim from Khawaja's book that sandpaper was also used there.

"It was given to me to take off," Sayers said on SEN Radio.

"That wasn't planned or anything. It was a wicket or drinks break after tea."

'Wrong' and 'nonsense' - Cummins on Khawaja claims

Australia doomed to live with stench of sandpapergate

Sayers also said there was a "60 to 90-minute" meeting in the Australia dressing room after Bancroft had been caught using sandpaper in Cape Town, in which players discussed taking collective responsibility - something Khawaja claims but Cummins said he did not remember in his extraordinary news conference on Friday.

"I am comfortable sitting here that I believe everyone in that side knew what was going on and what was being used," said Sayers, whose one Test was the final match of that series.

"It [sandpaper] was used in two Test matches and there were discussions in the changing rooms.

"I'm not taking sides, it's just my recollection of what took place.

"After the occurrence in Cape Town, we all sat in the changing rooms after that day's play and, probably for 60 to 90 minutes, we talked about what had happened and I guess where to next."

Sayers first backed Khawaja's recollections last week, saying "everything" in the former opener's book was "accurate".

In an episode which has dominated headlines in Australia and elsewhere, Khawaja said the entire Australia team knew about the plan to use sandpaper to tamper with the ball and should have taken responsibility.

Cummins, a bowler in that squad and now Australia captain, emphatically rejected the claims by calling them "100% wrong" and "utter nonsense".

The bowlers - Cummins, Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc and Nathan Lyon - have always claimed they did not know.

David Warner accused Cricket Australia of a "cover-up" on Saturday, suggesting Hazlewood, Starc and Lyon had not been interviewed as part of the governing body's investigation.

Warner, Bancroft and then captain Steve Smith served lengthy bans for their role in the scandal.

articles.title: Aaryavir Sehwag earns special two-word praise from Vaibhav Sooryavanshi
articles.summary: Aaryavir Sehwag enjoyed a memorable Under-19 Asia Cup campaign, earning recognition from fellow young sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi after helping India
articles.body: Aaryavir Sehwag enjoyed a memorable Under-19 Asia Cup campaign, earning recognition from fellow young sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi after helping India lift the title with a thrilling one-wicket victory over Pakistan.Sooryavanshi congratulated the son of former India opener Virender Sehwag through an Instagram story, sharing the tournament's leading run-scorers list with a simple message: "Star boiiiiii @aaryavirsehwag".The gesture was particularly interesting because Sooryavanshi, despite being just 15, has already established himself as one of India's most exciting young batting talents. His message was a nod to another youngster making waves in Indian cricket.Aaryavir thoroughly deserved the praise after finishing the tournament as its leading run-scorer. He collected 361 runs in five innings at an impressive average of 90.25, including one century and three half-centuries. His highest score was a magnificent 160 against the UAE.He was subsequently named Player of the Tournament.The youngster also delivered when it mattered most, scoring 58 off 61 balls against Pakistan in the final. His innings included nine boundaries and helped India build a strong foundation during their chase of 338. He shared a 95-run opening partnership with captain Lakshya Raichandani, who scored 80.Aaryavir also caught attention with his celebration after reaching his half-century, recreating Virat Kohli's famous 'bat does the talking' gesture. Despite taking a blow to his forearm and requiring medical attention, he continued batting and contributed significantly.Mohit Ulva seals dramatic India victoryThe final turned into a thrilling contest after Pakistan posted 337/9, powered by Usman Khan's 107. India found themselves struggling at 252/8 before Manal Chauhan (47 off 32) and Mohit Ulva (49 not out off 26) staged a remarkable recovery.With three runs required from the final delivery, Ulva smashed a boundary to secure a one-wicket victory and India's ninth Under-19 Asia Cup title.For Aaryavir, the tournament was a major breakthrough, while Sooryavanshi's congratulatory message added another memorable moment to his celebrations.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: WPL 2027: BCCI shifts Mumbai leg from Brabourne to Wankhede on ICC request; here's why
articles.summary: The Mumbai leg of the Women’s Premier League (WPL) 2027 will be held at the Wankhede Stadium instead of the Brabourne Stadium, the BCCI announced on
articles.body: The Mumbai leg of the Women’s Premier League (WPL) 2027 will be held at the Wankhede Stadium instead of the Brabourne Stadium, the BCCI announced on Sunday. The dates and fixtures of the tournament will remain unchanged.The fifth edition of the WPL will be played from January 14 to February 7, with Vadodara and Mumbai serving as the two host cities. The first leg will take place at the BCA Stadium in Vadodara from January 14 to 24, while Mumbai will host the remaining matches from January 26 until the final on February 7.The Mumbai leg was originally scheduled to be held at the Cricket Club of India’s (CCI) Brabourne Stadium. However, the venue has been changed as CCI is also set to host the inaugural edition of the ICC Women's Champions Trophy in the T20 format, which begins on February 14. The BCCI said the gap between the two tournaments would not give the pitches enough time to recover.“The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) has announced that the Mumbai leg of the Women’s Premier League 2027 will now be held at Wankhede Stadium, Mumbai, instead of the Brabourne Stadium at the Cricket Club of India (CCI). The dates and fixtures will remain unchanged,” the BCCI said in a statement.“The WPL Governing Council approved the original venues and dates for the fifth edition of the TATA WPL at its meeting on 15 September 2026. Under the approved schedule, the Mumbai leg, comprising Match Nos. 12 to 20, the Eliminator and the Final, was to be played at CCI between 26 January and 7 February 2027.”“As CCI is also scheduled to host the inaugural ICC Women’s Champions Trophy 2027, commencing on 14 February, the interval between the conclusion of the TATA WPL and the start of the multi-nation tournament would not provide sufficient time for the pitches to recover,” the board added.The BCCI said the venue was changed following a request from the International Cricket Council (ICC). The WPL Committee has approved the change, with Wankhede Stadium set to host all 11 matches of the Mumbai leg.“The change follows a request from the International Cricket Council (ICC) to shift the matches scheduled to be played at CCI. The WPL Committee has approved the change, with Wankhede Stadium now set to host all 11 matches of the Mumbai leg,” the BCCI said.The Mumbai Cricket Association (MCA), during its 95th Annual General Meeting, had formally requested the BCCI to consider it for hosting matches in case of changes to the schedules of future series.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Former India cricketer Sanjay Manjrekar took a swipe at the Indian Under-19 team's aggressive celebrations following their dramatic one-wicket victory
articles.body: Former India cricketer Sanjay Manjrekar took a swipe at the Indian Under-19 team's aggressive celebrations following their dramatic one-wicket victory over Pakistan in the Under-19 Asia Cup final on Saturday, suggesting that the young Indian players should pick opponents of their own size if they wanted to display aggression on the field.India pulled off a remarkable last-ball victory to reclaim the Under-19 Asia Cup title, chasing down a daunting target of 338 to beat Pakistan by one wicket in a thrilling final. The victory, however, was accompanied by an animated celebration from the Indian players, which caught Manjrekar's attention.Taking to X, the former India batter appeared to question the manner in which the young Indian team celebrated against Pakistan, describing the neighbouring country as a 'soft and easy target'."Indian cricket should now pick guys of their own size if they want to show ‘aggression’ on the field. Pak is now a soft & easy target.I suggest Aus, SA, NZ & Eng…" Manjrekar posted.The remarks came after India's dramatic victory, which was built on an extraordinary lower-order fightback after the team found itself in deep trouble during the chase.Defending champions Pakistan looked firmly in control when India slipped to 252/8 in the 42nd over while chasing 338. However, Manal Chauhan and Mohit Ulva turned the contest around with a crucial 57-run partnership for the ninth wicket.Manal scored 47 off 32 balls before departing with India still needing 36 runs with just one wicket remaining. Mohit, however, continued the fight, finding an unlikely partner in No. 11 C Venkata, who contributed an unbeaten 11 off eight deliveries.With eight runs required in the final over, the equation eventually came down to three off the last ball. Mohit kept his composure and smashed leg-spinner Ahmed Hussain wide of long-off for a boundary to seal India's title triumph.Mohit finished unbeaten on 49 off just 26 deliveries, while Manal's contribution proved equally crucial in India's stunning recovery.Earlier, skipper Lakshya Raichandani (80) and Aaryavir Sehwag (58) had provided India with a strong start, adding 95 runs for the opening wicket. But the dismissals of Sehwag, Raichandani and Anvay Dravid left India struggling before the lower order produced a remarkable turnaround.Pakistan had posted 337/9, courtesy of a century from Usman Khan (107) and a fluent 80 from Abdul Qadir. Captain Farhan Yousaf also chipped in with 60, while Kavya Patel claimed four wickets for India.The victory handed India the Under-19 Asia Cup title in dramatic fashion, but the celebrations also prompted a pointed reaction from Manjrekar on social media.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Mount Maunganui: "Not again... we just settled," said a group of fans on the grass banks enjoying the afternoon sun before another set exclaimed, "even the fizz of the beer is still alive". There was collective exasperation when Rohit Sharma dragged himself back to the changing room after another poor outing in New Zealand. For the repeat spectators at the Bay Oval, this must have been deja vu; they had seen the former captain dismissed early within three days.For over a decade, Indian cricket has witnessed a trend: the first wicket brings out a cheer with Virat Kohli’s arrival raising expectations and excitement. But in this five-match ODI series, even those cheers have been short-lived, and the feeling quickly turned into disappointment. And then embarrassment.It's been the story of the ODI leg of the tour. Batting techniques have been exposed, shot selections questioned, and players haven't remained in the middle long enough.The build-up to the series was dominated by the inexperienced bowling attack, but as curtains drew on the five-ODI affair, it has shifted to how the famed India line-up staged a meek surrender. The conditions were testing, the weather unpredictable, and the opposition attack hostile. But it was worrying to see how the batting folded.For the first time since 1985, no India batter managed a series haul of 100 runs in a five-ODI series. Virat Kohli's 86 tops the charts and 74 of those runs came in the series opener in Auckland. That knock was also the only fifty-plus score by an Indian batter in the four ODIs they played. Not just Rohit and Kohli, even Shreyas Iyer and Axar Patel struggled to get going. Shubman Gill also scored 37 runs (in 2 innings) before shifting focus to the Test series preparations in Wellington.The underlying theme for the series has largely remained that these conditions are the closest to what one could expect in South Africa for the World Cup. The performances give little confidence and head coach Gautam Gambhir's assessment after the fourth ODI hinted that the alarm bells are ringing."You are always concerned when you get bundled out for 90-odd. Why won't I be concerned?" Gambhir had said during the post-match press conference. "I think I will be concerned because obviously these are conditions which are going to be closest to what we might get during the World Cup."When you play in India, obviously you all know that there is hardly anything for the bowlers, but when you come in these conditions, you know that there is actually a good contest between bat and ball, so this is probably the closest, so obviously I would be concerned because not only in this game, but even in the previous game, we were 7 down for 111-112, so for me I think the bigger concern is not the runs, it's how quickly we got bundled out - I think in around 26 or 27 overs, so hopefully we can try and rectify that as soon as possible."Gambhir's hopes for a turnaround in the final fixture went up in smoke as a similar script unfolded at the Bay Oval, even while batting first with the sun out in its full glory. More than the pitch playing its tricks or the bowlers being unplayable, the issue was the circumspect approach and questionable shot selections. Rohit went early into the flick, Kohli played a rash shot, Ruturaj Gaikwad looked good but perished driving, and Shreyas Iyer departed to a short ball again.It has been a collective batting failure, and even if the series against Sri Lanka and Zimbabwe sees them back amongst the runs, the frailties away from home will need serious introspection. For starters, the team management must press for lively pitches in the six ODIs preceding the IPL, as flat tracks serve no purpose other than inflating averages and giving a false sense of optimism."Kya hi hoga inka World Cup mai? (what will happen to them during the World Cup?)... inko highway pe hi khilao (make them play on flat pitches only)," was the mood in the lawns behind the stadium. The Indian fans, who had gathered in large numbers, didn't have good memories to take home but offered a collective warning to avoid awakening ghosts of the away past.Brief Scores: India 209 in 42.1 overs (Axar Patel 46, Ishan Kishan 46; Mitchell Santner 3/47, Jacob Duffy 3/60) beat New Zealand 187 in 48.1 overs (Dean Foxcroft 31; Arshdeep Singh 3/30) by 22 runs.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Arshdeep Singh & Co. swing it India's way to secure 3-1 series win
articles.summary: Mount Maunganui: The dhol beats synced with Arshdeep Singh's run-up as he steamed in to bowl the final over his spell.
articles.body: Mount Maunganui: The dhol beats synced with Arshdeep Singh's run-up as he steamed in to bowl the final over his spell. India were three wickets away from a win, and Shreyas Iyer rolled the dice hoping to pick a crucial wicket. Two steps in, both Arshdeep and the dhol missed their beat, forcing the left-arm bowler to abort his run-up and restart. He returned to the top of his mark and did exactly what was expected: pick a wicket and keep the visitors in striking distance of a famous win.With eight wickets down, India had their tails up and both the DJ and crowd joined in to lift the mood at the Bay Oval. The hands which were earlier warming inside the pockets were now applauding the bowling attack for its lion-hearted performance. The equation was delicately placed at 37 runs needed off 30 balls when Iyer turned to Mohammed Siraj, bowling his final over, in search of the last two wickets. Only Yash Thakur's one over and spin bowling remained for the last four wickets, and those were truly the most important six deliveries of the match for India.He nearly got the job done but Ishan Kishan misjudged an edge behind the stumps and the ball raced to the boundary. The frustration was evident in the Indian camp, as the majority of the remaining bowling would be spin. Then Axar Patel came in and struck on the second delivery, leaving India just one wicket away from a hard-fought win. New Zealand survived Yash Thakur's final over but Axar picked the final wicket to help India register a 22-run win.Not just in this game but the entire series, especially in the absence of Jasprit Bumrah, Prasidh Krishna, Gurnoor Brar, Auqib Nabi, Mohammed Siraj and Yash Thakur stepped up, receiving able support from the spin of Axar Patel and Naman Dhir.Defending a 210-run target, the focus was never on saving runs but on pressing for ten wickets. Iyer attacked with his wicket-taking options, even if it meant bowling out Arshdeep in the 43rd over and introducing spin for the first time in the 36th over of New Zealand's innings.Much like the fourth ODI, the golden hour injected fresh life into the surface and India exerted enough pressure by picking wickets at regular intervals. The tight lines ensured the run-rate was never in comfortable territory during the run-chase. It was a good old-fashioned ODI fixture but both teams had their moments and momentum kept shifting either way.But the evening breeze and the relentlessness of the inexperienced bowling attack plastered over the batting cracks, helping India stage an emphatic fight, seal the series 3-1 and complete the white-ball leg with two trophies in the cabinet.Brief Scores: India 209 in 42.1 overs (Axar Patel 46, Ishan Kishan 46; Mitchell Santner 3/47, Jacob Duffy 3/60) beat New Zealand 187 in 48.1 overs (Dean Foxcroft 31; Arshdeep Singh 3/30) by 22 runs.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: First-ball duck! Mahfijul Islam suffers Test debut nightmare as Kagiso Rabada scripts rare bowling record
articles.summary: Bangladesh debutant Mahfijul Islam endured a nightmare start to his Test career, while South Africa speedster Kagiso Rabada etched his name into the
articles.body: Bangladesh debutant Mahfijul Islam endured a nightmare start to his Test career, while South Africa speedster Kagiso Rabada etched his name into the record books with a rare first-ball dismissal in the opening Test at the Wanderers Stadium on Sunday.Mahfijul was dismissed for a golden duck off the very first legal delivery of the match, becoming the first Bangladesh batter and only the fourth player in Test history to be dismissed off the opening ball of a Test on debut.The left-handed batter, drafted into the playing XI as a replacement for the injured Shadman Islam, edged a delivery from Rabada that seamed away and was caught in the slips. His dismissal handed Rabada an immediate breakthrough and left Bangladesh reeling at the start of their innings.The unwanted record had previously been registered by South Africa's Jimmy Cook, who fell to Kapil Dev in Durban in 1992, West Indies' Leon Garrick, dismissed by Allan Donald in Kingston in 2001, and Afghanistan's Abdul Malik, who was dismissed by Blessing Muzarabani in Abu Dhabi in 2019.Rabada joins elite South African listWhile Mahfijul's dismissal marked a forgettable beginning to his international career, Rabada's first-ball breakthrough brought him a place in an exclusive group of South African bowlers.He became only the fourth South African to take a wicket with the first legal delivery of a men's Test match, joining Bert Vogler, Allan Donald and Dale Steyn.Vogler was the first to achieve the feat, dismissing England's Tom Hayward with the opening delivery of the Oval Test in 1907. Donald followed suit when he removed Garrick in the Kingston Test in 2001.Steyn then joined the list in 2010, dismissing England opener Andrew Strauss with the first ball of a Test match. Rabada has now become the latest Proteas fast bowler to achieve the distinction.Bangladesh collapse after early Rabada strikesThe early breakthrough was the beginning of a difficult opening session for Bangladesh, who opted to bat after winning the toss.Rabada struck again almost immediately, dismissing Mominul Haque for a duck to leave the visitors at 2/2. He then removed Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain Shanto in the ninth over, reducing them to 22/3 and putting South Africa firmly in control.Bangladesh were chasing their first-ever Test victory over South Africa. They had lost 14 of their previous 16 meetings, with the remaining two ending in draws.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'I've got a really nice partner': Arshdeep Singh opens up about fiancee after India's dramatic series triumph
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Arshdeep Singh had plenty to celebrate after playing a decisive role in India's thrilling 22-run victory over New Zealand in the fifth ODI in
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Arshdeep Singh had plenty to celebrate after playing a decisive role in India's thrilling 22-run victory over New Zealand in the fifth ODI in Mount Maunganui on Sunday, but the Player of the Match had another special reason to cherish the moment. The left-arm pacer opened up about his fiancee, crediting her support for helping him maintain the right mindset and perform on the field.Arshdeep, who finished with impressive figures of 3/30, spoke warmly about his partner after India defended a modest total of 209 to secure a dramatic victory and clinched the five-match ODI series 3-1."I mean, God has been really grateful and kind to me. I've got a really nice partner. She's very supportive and always helps me stay in the right mindset. So yes, a lot credit goes to her as well, the way I am on the field depends a lot on how I'm working off the field. So yes, it's been very exciting and I'm loving it," Arshdeep said after the match.The Indian pacer also reflected on his recent engagement at Mount Maunganui beach, admitting that he was nervous before popping the question but had the perfect setting to make the occasion memorable."Can't ask for a better view to do that. I was pretty tense but yes, the view helped and it feels pretty nice," he said.Arshdeep's crucial cameo and disciplined bowlingWhile his comments about his fiancee offered a glimpse into his personal life, Arshdeep's contribution with the ball and a handy cameo with the bat were equally important in India's comeback victory.The left-arm pacer chipped in with crucial runs alongside Mohammed Siraj towards the end of India's innings, helping the visitors cross the 200-run mark after New Zealand had dominated with the ball.Explaining the importance of their partnership, Arshdeep said: "Yes, that's the chat when we ended the batting as well. Siraj told me that these runs will be very crucial. And we made sure we went above 200 and that was a little thought in mind: we had crossed a small milestone there and had some runs to bowl at."The 27-year-old also joked about his enthusiasm for batting, despite coming in at No. 11."I love my batting. Even if I'm batting at eleven, I enjoy it. And always trying to create room for myself and smash it. But some people on my team say that I'm scared of the ball. But I take it. I create room," he said.With the ball, Arshdeep was instrumental in turning the contest around after New Zealand had reached 64/1 in their chase. India picked up five wickets for just 55 runs to shift the momentum before eventually bowling out the hosts for 187 in 48.1 overs.Reflecting on the bowling unit's persistence, he said: "I feel like we kept coming and we were very disciplined with our areas and we didn't let go of that thing even when we were not getting the results, we were not getting the wickets. But we kept bowling that and eventually got the results and yes, we won."India's pacers script remarkable turnaroundIndia had earlier struggled with the bat after being put in, with Matthew Fisher removing Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli cheaply. Axar Patel and Ishan Kishan scored 46 each, while Naman Dhir added 22 as the visitors were bowled out for 209.New Zealand appeared well placed during their chase, but India's bowlers produced a collective effort to trigger a dramatic collapse.Yash Thakur claimed his maiden ODI wicket, while Mohammed Siraj and Axar picked up two wickets apiece. Arshdeep led the attack with three scalps to complete India's turnaround.The two sides will next meet in a two-Test series beginning November 19.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'It was a series for bowlers, not batters': Shreyas Iyer after India's 3-1 ODI series win over New Zealand
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India captain Shreyas Iyer described the ODI series against New Zealand as one dominated by bowlers, praising his team's ability to adapt to
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India captain Shreyas Iyer described the ODI series against New Zealand as one dominated by bowlers, praising his team's ability to adapt to challenging conditions and deliver when it mattered. India secured a 22-run victory in the fifth ODI at Bay Oval on Sunday, defending a modest total of 209 to clinch the five-match series 3-1.Reflecting on the series, Iyer said: “It was a series for bowlers, not for batters. Everyone stood up to the occasion.”Iyer also spoke about his experience leading India in the ODI format, describing it as both challenging and exhausting, but an exciting experience. He felt the series presented different phases, with the game slowing down at certain points and testing the team's ability to assess the pace of the contest.“I enjoyed leading in ODI. Challenging, exhausting… there was a period where the game went slow. That's how you gauge the pace. Exciting. One win, one loss, 50-50!” he said.Despite being bowled out for 89 in the fourth ODI, India responded strongly in the series decider. Iyer said the team was determined to give its best and did not need an extensive discussion at the halfway stage, despite having only 209 runs on the board.“We wanted to give everything and there was no major discussion at the halfway mark,” he explained.On his bowling strategy, Iyer revealed that he continued with his planned combination of seamers, trusting them to build pressure and take wickets through partnerships.“I stuck with the plan of seamers and wickets kept coming. When bowlers bowled in partnerships, you bowl tight from one end and pick wicket from the other,” he said.India's seamers justified that approach, restricting New Zealand to 187 in 49 overs. Arshdeep Singh led the attack with three wickets for 30 runs, while the bowling unit prevented the hosts from building momentum during the middle overs.Looking ahead, Iyer acknowledged that the upcoming conditions in South Africa would present a different challenge, particularly with changing weather and conditions. He also pointed out that batting had been difficult for both sides throughout the contest.“You never know what will happen in South Africa. Weather will be different. Batting didn't happen from both teams… wicket was for bowlers. Most important is to win series and we won,” Iyer said.The Indian captain also addressed the team's response to its heavy defeat in the fourth ODI, where Matt Henry's bowling proved particularly difficult to handle. Iyer said the side quickly put the loss behind them rather than allowing it to affect their preparations for the decider.“We forgot about the fourth ODI loss the next day. Matt Henry was bowling gas… he was lethal. We accepted and moved on,” he added.India's victory in the final ODI completed a successful campaign, with the team overcoming difficult batting conditions and a crushing defeat to finish the series with a 3-1 result.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Former Pakistan captain Mohammad Yousuf has criticised the Indian Under-19 team's aggressive celebrations following their dramatic one-wicket victory over
articles.body: Former Pakistan captain Mohammad Yousuf has criticised the Indian Under-19 team's aggressive celebrations following their dramatic one-wicket victory over Pakistan in the Under-19 Asia Cup final, reminding the young cricketers that they represent not just their country but also their upbringing and values.Yousuf urged the youngsters to remain respectful and composed in both victory and defeat, saying that true sportsmanship is reflected in how players conduct themselves on the field, irrespective of the result.His remarks came after videos of India's celebrations following Saturday's thrilling final went viral on social media. Several Indian players, including Manal Chauhan, Mohit Ulva and Chigurupati Venkata, were seen making aggressive gestures towards their Pakistani counterparts. As tensions escalated on the field, members of India's support staff had to intervene and pull the youngsters away to calm the situation.Taking to social media, Yousuf acknowledged India's victory but used the occasion to deliver a message on sportsmanship and player conduct."The #U19WorldCup has come to an end, and as usual, #India got the better of #Pakistan under pressure. It was a great learning platform for both teams and for players who have the potential to become future stars," he wrote."One thing I would like to say is that when you play sports or compete at any level, you are not just representing your country. In fact, you are representing your upbringing, the values, and the ethics your parents taught you as a child. Therefore, always remain respectful and composed, whether in victory or defeat. True sportsmanship is reflected in the way you conduct yourself, regardless of the outcome. Role model legends #sachin & #Saeedanwar," he added.The comments have added to the debate surrounding the conduct of the young Indian players after a final that witnessed high drama at both ends of the contest.India's triumph was particularly remarkable given the position they found themselves in during the chase. Asked to chase 338, India were struggling at 252/8 in the 42nd over before Manal Chauhan and Mohit Ulva produced a remarkable fightback.The pair stitched together 57 runs for the ninth wicket, with Manal scoring 47 off 32 balls and Mohit remaining unbeaten on 49 off just 26 deliveries. Manal departed with India still requiring 36 runs and only one wicket in hand.Mohit then found support in No. 11 batter C Venkata, who scored an unbeaten 11 off eight balls. With eight runs needed in the final over, the equation came down to three off the last delivery. Mohit smashed leg-spinner Ahmed Hussain wide of long-off for a boundary to seal India's 339/9 and a memorable one-wicket victory.Earlier, Pakistan had posted 337/9, riding on Usman Khan's 107 and Abdul Qadir's 80. Captain Farhan Yousaf also contributed 60, while Kavya Patel claimed four wickets for India.The victory helped India reclaim the Under-19 Asia Cup title, but the celebrations that followed have since become a talking point, with Yousuf joining those questioning the young players' on-field behaviour.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: England set up ODI series decider vs Australia after Tom Banton and Gus Atkinson fire in victory at Adelaide Oval
articles.summary: Tom Banton scores second ODI ton as England hit record 355-6 in Australia before Gus Atkinson and Sonny Baker reduce home side to 29-4; Mitch Marsh's hosts - who rested Mahli Beardman following six-wicket haul in the series opener - now meet England in winner-takes-all clash on Wednesday
articles.body:
A touring side rolled for 131 in Friday's opener at Perth posted their highest ODI total in Australia, with a score of 355-6 underpinned by Banton's 121 from 99 balls and featuring fifties for Jordan Cox (67 off 49), Joe Root (62 off 68) and Will Jacks (54no off 40).

England lost their fourth wicket in the 35th over - Banton holing out immediately after back-to-back sixes - whereas Australia lost their fourth at the end of the seventh with just 29 runs on the board, before being dismissed for 220 in 44.3 overs with Atkinson claiming 4-28 and Jofra Archer (1-26) taking the final wicket.

The ODI finale at Ninja Stadium in Tasmania next week (3.30am start UK on Wednesday) is now winner-takes-all, ahead of the sides moving on to a five-match T20 international series, starting at the Melbourne Cricket Ground next Saturday (8.15am UK time).

In Sunday's match, Australia were reeling on 13-3 after three wickets for no runs in six balls as Atkinson had Travis Head (7) and Cooper Connolly (0) caught at slip in the same over before captain Mitchell Marsh (2) perished the same way off Sonny Baker (1-45).

When Josh Inglis (3) became the fourth man caught behind, off Atkinson after a successful review, Marsh's men looked to have little hope of completing their highest successful run chase at home.

Matt Renshaw (63) and Cameron Green (64) rebuilt with a fifth-wicket stand of 98, during which Renshaw was dropped on 27 by Jacks at cover and Green inexplicably grassed on seven at deep midwicket by Liam Dawson (2-41), the player who eventually broke the partnership when he pinned Renshaw lbw on the reverse sweep.

Green went on to be stumped in bizarre fashion as a delivery from Dawson ricocheted off wicketkeeper Cox's pads and back onto the stumps, while Sam Curran (2-38) was on a hat-trick after ousting Jack Edwards (17) with a moon ball and then Xavier Bartlett (0).

With the ball, Australia missed Mahli Beardman, who ripped through the away side with 6-24 at Optus Stadium two days earlier but was rested on Sunday, with the hosts taking a cautious approach with a quick whose young career has been hit by injury.

Banton is likely to line up in the middle order in the T20 series but has seemingly cinched a long-term spot in the ODI XI as opener after yet another impressive showing.

The Somerset batter has registered two hundreds and four fifties in nine innings since replacing the injured Jacob Bethell (knee) as Ben Duckett's top-order partner at the back end of the home summer, with this latest ton coming from a brisk 85 deliveries.

Banton was struck on the grille by a sharp bouncer from Beardman's replacement Riley Meredith early in his innings but he brushed off that blow to club many of his 16 boundaries (12 fours, four sixes) leg-side off the short deliveries Australia targeted him with.

Banton put on 137 with Root from 19-1, after Duckett clothed to point, and it was somewhat of a surprise when Root, perhaps looking to up the run rate, top-edged spinner Connolly into the off-side on the pull having been typically calm before then.

When England skipper Harry Brook (5) chopped on trying to scoop Meredith over fine leg and Banton's fine innings came to a close following a diving catch from Green in the deep, the visitors could have wobbled - but they didn't as the lower middle order fired.

Cox and Jacks dug in initially, before helping their team plunder 110 runs from the final 10 overs, a passage of play in which Curran (14 off 9) chipped in and Atkinson (13no off 4) belted Edwards for two sixes in an 18-run 50th over that concluded with a Jacks four.

It was then over to Atkinson and Baker with the ball - the latter given the new pill ahead of Archer - as Australia's top four each fell for single digits after playing flat-footed swats against back-of-a-length deliveries.

Their departures meant the result never looked in significant doubt and if England's catching had been on point - Root also dropped Inglis on one at slip - the margin of victory would have been even steeper.

Brook delighted by England bouncing back

England captain Harry Brook, speaking at the presentation:

"I think we put in a really good performance there and it was really pleasing to see us bounce back [from the heavy defeat in Perth].

"We looked in control throughout the whole batting innings, countering their bad balls and putting them under pressure when we needed to.

"Banton played an exceptional innings, sticking to his strengths, and the depth we have means we were able to go on and get 350.

"[In the field], this is the template we want to set in every game. Bar a few dropped catches, it was awesome.

"A massive discussion in the group for a year and a half has been about wanting to be one of the best fielding sides in the world, one of the fittest and strongest sides in the world."

Marsh: England showed they are 'well rounded'

Australia captain Mitchell Marsh, speaking at the presentation:

"We bowled first thinking there might be a little bit in the wicket - which sounds weird to say at Adelaide Oval - and to maximise the first 20 overs, but England batted really well.

"I thought we tried a lot with the ball, a few different plans, like Riley Meredith bowling bumpers, but we knew England are a well-rounded side and they showed that today.

"With the bat, when you are chasing 350, you are under the pump from ball one and we needed two of the top four to go big and lay a platform."

Results/schedule for England's Australia tour

ODIs 3.30am UK time, with T20s 8.15am UK time

Third ODI: Wednesday November 18 (Hobart)

First T20I: Saturday November 21 (Melbourne)

Second T20I: Tuesday November 24 (Carrara)

Third T20I: Friday November 27 (Brisbane)

Fourth T20I: Sunday November 29 (Sydney)

Fifth T20I: Wednesday December 2 (Canberra)

articles.title: Australia vs England: Tom Banton, Gus Atkinson and Sonny Baker impress as tourists level series
articles.summary: Tom Banton scores a century and Sonny Baker and Gus Atkinson impress with the ball as England's wildly inconsistent one-day team hammer Australia.
articles.body:
England 355-6 (50 overs): Banton 121, Cox 67, Root 62

Australia 220 all out (44.3 overs): Green 64, Renshaw 63; Atkinson 4-28

England won by 135 runs; series level at 1-1

Tom Banton scored a century and Sonny Baker and Gus Atkinson impressed with the ball as England's wildly inconsistent one-day team hammered Australia to set up a series decider.

Banton scored a fine 121 – pushing his case for selection further with a second ODI hundred – in England's 355-6.

After being knocked over for 131 two days ago in Perth, England's total was their highest in one-day internationals in Australia.

And then their bowlers, who failed to defend 430 against Sri Lanka last month and were undone by an improbable last-wicket partnership against Pakistan, reduced Australia to 29-4 inside seven overs and easily closed out a 135-run victory.

The win ends a seven-match losing run against Australia across formats in Adelaide - and a run of six consecutive defeats by Australia in 50-over cricket away from home.

But, more significantly, it corrects their course after those damaging defeats against Sri Lanka, Pakistan and Australia and offers positives amid the frustrations going into the decider on Wednesday (03:30 GMT) in Hobart.

Curran's best weapon? The moon ball strikes again

TMS podcast: Banton blasts England to victory in Adelaide

Will the real England please stand up? Before those defeats in Rawalpindi, Lahore and Perth, England had won three ODI series this year.

This win only adds to the feeling they are extremely difficult to figure out.

Banton was superb and, even more encouragingly, Atkinson and Baker were too.

This England team has often struggled for new-ball wickets and Baker, brought in for Jamie Overton in an attempt to correct that fault, found significant swing. He took the key wicket of Australia captain Mitchell Marsh, taken high at slip by a diving Joe Root, for two.

Atkinson used nip to nick off Travis Head for seven – the second match in a row he has dismissed the Australia left-hander – and also have both Cooper Connolly and Josh Inglis caught behind. Career-best figures of 4-28 are reward for good recent performance that have often gone unrewarded.

England were not perfect. They dropped four catches – first Inglis and then Matt Renshaw and Cameron Green, who made 63 and 64 respectively to drag out Australia's score.

But by the end, Sam Curran had taken two wickets in two balls, including bowling Jack Edwards with his moon ball, in a boost after his poor run.

Green was also out stumped when the ball deflected off Jordan Cox's shin and onto the stumps and Liam Dawson took 2-41 as he was preferred again to Adil Rashid.

These are the performances that suggest England can challenge at next year's World Cup, but plenty more are needed.

Banton's chance as opener has come courtesy of Jacob Bethell's knee injury. In nine innings, he has scored four fifties and two hundreds. The spot should now be his going forward.

The 28-year-old right-hander was hit on the helmet on 10 by left-armer Spencer Johnson but afterwards attacked Adelaide's short square boundaries with his pull.

A partnership of 137 with Joe Root was steady and important – given Ben Duckett had slashed to point for nine and the recent memory of Perth.

It was Banton's hundred, 67 from 49 balls by Cox and 54 not out by Will Jacks that, with Australia's match-winner from the first ODI, Mahli Beardman, rested, took England to a dominant position, however.

Cox came in after captain Harry Brook, on five, deflected the ball onto his stumps when trying a ramp to push on the scoring. Jacks joined him when Banton holed out at deep square-leg after one too many of those pulls.

Cox and Jacks were scoring at a run a ball when taking England to 245-4 after 40 overs but together helped their side take 110 from the last.

Cox, after a run of lower scores as he fills in for Jos Buttler, drove, cut, scooped and pulled. A reverse scoop for four off Xavier Bartlett was outrageous.

He has one more chance in this series to push his case further - possibly more if Buttler does not recovery for the January series against South Africa.

"Banton has really found his flow for batting," former England captain Michael Vaughan said.

"I don't know who the person was to say 'you can open the batting in 50-over cricket, Tom' but it's been a tremendous move. He and Ben Duckett look a good combo.

"Banton seems to have all the time, all the strokes. He's got the pull shot, he's got the drive down the ground and he plays spin great. He hasn't looked like he's trying to hard to score runs, he's just batted."

articles.body: New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner credited India's disciplined bowling attack for making the most of the conditions in the fifth ODI, as the visitors defended a modest target of 210 to seal a 22-run victory and wrap up the five-match series 3-1 on Sunday.India were bowled out for 209 in 42.1 overs at Bay Oval, but their bowlers produced a collective effort to dismiss the hosts for 187 in 48.1 overs. The result handed India their third ODI series triumph in New Zealand.While Santner was pleased with his team's efforts to restrict India to a manageable total, he admitted that New Zealand failed to make their batting partnerships count during the chase. He also praised stand-in captain Shreyas Iyer for his bowling changes and the way he managed the Indian attack."I think they bowled really well in a tonight show. All four seamers bowled well; Shreyas did a great job rotating them around. Obviously held Axar back because the seamers were going really well. And I think, you know, they were able to chip wickets away through the middle as well. I think if we had taken each partnership a little bit longer, we would have won that game. But there was definitely some tricky periods. They brought Arshdeep back on at the right time and Siraj as well. So it was a great bowling performance," Santner said during the post-match press conference.The New Zealand skipper felt the pitch had something in it for the bowlers, but was satisfied with how his side adapted after being asked to bowl first. He singled out Michael Bracewell's contribution in the middle overs and believed his team had done enough to keep India to a competitive total."I was very happy at the halfway stage. It’s probably not as much in it as we thought. I thought the guys adapted well. It was obviously a little bit slow and then the way Beast (Michael Bracewell) kind of operated through the middle, you know, was outstanding. I think we were able to chip wickets out throughout. I was pretty happy with the 200 (209)," he said.However, New Zealand could not build the partnerships required to stay on course in the chase, with India's bowlers consistently applying pressure. Santner felt the visitors used the two-paced nature of the surface and its bounce effectively."I think it was, I think with the fields, it was a little bit two paced, the pitch. And I thought they squeezed us pretty well. And they made great use of the bounce as well," he added.Despite losing the series 3-1, Santner believed the margin did not accurately capture the competitiveness of the contests. He pointed to rain interruptions, tosses going against his side and opportunities given to different players as factors that shaped the series."You look at the scoreline 3-1. I think it was closer than that. We played some good cricket. Obviously had a little bit of rain around and lost a few tosses. But in between all that, there’s a lot of good stuff. I think today, even in the last game, if you could take it a little bit deeper, there’s obviously a lot of time, especially with the bat in 50-over cricket. And then, different guys coming in, it’s obviously good experience. Guys stepped up as well, which was nice," he said.Arshdeep Singh led India's bowling effort with figures of 3/30, while Mohammed Siraj and Axar Patel picked up two wickets apiece. Auqib Nabi, Yash Thakur and Naman Dhir also contributed with a wicket each. Dean Foxcroft top-scored for New Zealand with 31, while Santner managed 24 before the hosts were bowled out short of the target.Santner also gave an update on the hand injury he suffered while batting during the chase. The New Zealand captain was struck on the hand and needed treatment from the team's physiotherapist."Pretty sore, not a lot (smiles), it's not great. An x-ray tomorrow morning, let's see what it is," he said.Earlier, India had struggled to put up a substantial total after being sent in to bat. Ishan Kishan and Axar Patel scored 46 each, while Shreyas Iyer made 22. Santner and Jacob Duffy claimed three wickets apiece, with Matthew Fisher taking two.The victory marked India's third ODI series win on New Zealand soil, adding to their previous triumphs in 2009 and the 2018-19 season.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: England hit back with 135-run thrashing of Australia! Tom Banton's ton powers visitors to series-levelling win
articles.summary: England produced a stunning response to their opening-match defeat, hammering Australia by 135 runs in the second ODI at Adelaide Oval on Sunday to level
articles.body: England produced a stunning response to their opening-match defeat, hammering Australia by 135 runs in the second ODI at Adelaide Oval on Sunday to level the three-match series 1-1. Tom Banton led the charge with a magnificent century as the visitors posted their highest-ever ODI total on Australian soil before their bowlers dismantled the home side's batting line-up.After being thrashed by seven wickets in a low-scoring contest in Perth, England bounced back emphatically, piling up 355/6 after being asked to bat first. Banton anchored the innings with a brilliant 121 off 99 deliveries, while Joe Root (62), Jamie Cox (67) and Will Jacks (54 not out) provided valuable contributions to take the visitors to an imposing total.Australia's bowlers struggled to contain England's aggressive approach, with the visitors building momentum through crucial partnerships and accelerating towards the end of their innings.Banton's innings proved the difference, earning him the Player of the Match award and giving England the platform they needed to turn the series around.Banton leads England's batting charge with brilliant centuryPlaying his first match at Adelaide Oval, Banton made the occasion memorable with a composed yet attacking knock.The right-hander spoke about the experience of playing at the iconic venue and adapting his approach to the demands of 50-over cricket."It's my first time in Adelaide. I've watched a lot of cricket in Australia over the years, the Ashes, white-ball series. So, to come here today is a pretty special feeling," Banton said.Reflecting on his batting approach, he added: "50-over cricket is hard. Sometimes you get off to a flyer and then you've got to rein it back in. And vice versa."Root also praised Banton for converting a good start into a substantial innings, highlighting the importance of partnerships in setting up a competitive total."You know how important partnerships are in this format and making sure you can set the game up towards the back end. And I thought we did that really well," Root said."But for Tom to go on and make it really count after a really solid start was fantastic. I'm really pleased for him. He works incredibly hard and he sort of got his opportunity and really taken it at the top of the order."Root also reflected on his 15-year international career and his role in a relatively inexperienced England side."I also dropped one. So still plenty of work to be done there. But still love playing, love being involved in this team. Obviously, it's quite a young team, it's quite inexperienced," he said.England bowlers trigger Australia's collapseChasing 356, Australia suffered a disastrous start under the Adelaide lights as England's new-ball bowlers exploited movement in the air and off the surface.The hosts slumped to 29/4 inside seven overs, with Gus Atkinson leading the demolition job by claiming three early wickets.Matt Renshaw and Cameron Green attempted to revive Australia's innings, putting together a 98-run partnership and scoring half-centuries. However, their resistance never threatened to take the game away from England.Renshaw eventually fell to Liam Dawson while attempting a reverse sweep, before Sam Curran struck twice in successive deliveries to remove Edwards and Bartlett.Green was then dismissed in the following over in an unusual stumping, leaving Australia with little hope of mounting a comeback.The lower order offered some resistance, with Adam Zampa, Mahli Beardman, Mitchell Johnson and Riley Meredith reaching double figures, but the damage had already been done.Australia were eventually bowled out for 220 in 44.3 overs, handing England a comprehensive 135-run victory.The result sets up a series decider in the third ODI, with England having successfully erased their Perth disappointment to draw level at 1-1.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India fight back to end New Zealand's long unbeaten run in home ODI series with 22-run victory at Mount Maunganui
articles.summary: India's Arshdeep Singh, Mohammed Siraj and Axar Patel make vital contributions with bat and ball as New Zealand lose home ODI series for first time since 2019; Kiwis had won 11 bilateral contests in a row on own turf before 3-1 defeat; teams now meet in two Tests, starting on November 19
articles.body:
The visitors slumped to 34-3 - albeit better than the 0-3 where they found themselves during a 244-run thrashing in the fourth ODI at the same venue on Friday - and later lost four wickets for 23 runs to be bowled out for 209 after losing the toss at Bay Oval.

However, the 26 runs put on in partnership between last-wicket pair Arshdeep Singh (14) and Mohammed Siraj (14) proved crucial after that duo bagged five wickets between them - Arshdeep bagging 3-30 and Siraj 2-50 - to skittle the Black Caps for 187 in reply.

New Zealand had already seen India end their streak of 11 straight home bilateral ODI series victories but would have had the consolation of a 2-2 draw had they produced a successful chase and looked poised to do that before losing 5-55 from 64-1.

India's spin-bowling all-rounder Axar Patel followed his innings of 46 - he joint top-scored in the match alongside team-mate Ishan Kishan - with figures of 2-28 from 6.1 overs as the tourists claimed the series 3-1.

The Kiwis' woes began when Will Young (22) was caught off Arshdeep by Ruturaj Gaikwad at deep square, with top-scorer Dean Foxcroft (31) sixth out when he chopped Yash Thakur (1-38) onto his stumps to hand the India debutant his maiden ODI scalp.

Thakur's strike meant India claimed two wickets in as many balls, with Auqib Nabi removing Michael Bracewell (19) from the previous delivery, caught at deep midwicket.

New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner (24) and Kristian Clarke (16) put on 39 for the seventh wicket from 119-6 but when Santner was out slog-sweeping Naman Dhir (1-4) and Clarke snicked Arshdeep behind, Axar polished off the tail.

New Zealand lost the preceding T20I series 3-2.

The Kiwis will now host India in two Tests, starting in Wellington on November 19 ahead of a second fixture in Christchurch from November 27.

articles.title: Joe Root scripts history against Australia, achieves first-ever feat for England in ODIs
articles.summary: Joe Root added another milestone to his remarkable ODI career on Sunday, becoming the first England batter to score 50 half-centuries in the format during
articles.body: Joe Root added another milestone to his remarkable ODI career on Sunday, becoming the first England batter to score 50 half-centuries in the format during the second match against Australia in Adelaide.Batting at No. 3 after Australia captain Mitchell Marsh elected to field, Root scored 62 off 68 deliveries to help England post a formidable 355/6 at the Adelaide Oval. He brought up his half-century in 50 balls in the 22nd over, reaching a landmark that no other English batter has achieved in ODI cricket.Root, England's leading run-scorer in ODIs, now has 50 fifties and 20 centuries in 201 appearances. His tally of 70 scores of 50 or more is also the highest by an English batter in the format.The 35-year-old is comfortably ahead of former England captain Eoin Morgan, who finished his ODI career with 42 half-centuries from 225 matches. Ian Bell occupies third place with 35, while Jos Buttler has 30.Most half-centuries for England in ODIsPlayerMatchesRuns100s50sJoe Root2018,0892050Eoin Morgan2256,9571342Ian Bell1615,416435Jos Buttler2045,6781130Root's latest achievement also places him among an elite group in international one-day cricket. The overall record for the most ODI half-centuries remains with former India great Sachin Tendulkar, who accumulated 96 fifties in 463 matches between 1989 and 2012, alongside 49 hundreds.Sri Lanka's Kumar Sangakkara is second on the all-time list with 93 half-centuries, followed by South Africa's Jacques Kallis with 86. Former India captain Rahul Dravid and Pakistan's Inzamam-ul-Haq have 83 each, while Australia's Ricky Ponting finished with 82.Virat Kohli is next on the list among active-era greats, with 80 half-centuries and 55 centuries in 322 ODIs.Most half-centuries in ODI cricketPlayerTeamMatchesRuns100s50sSachin TendulkarIndia46318,4264996Kumar SangakkaraSri Lanka40414,2342593Jacques KallisSouth Africa32811,5791786Rahul DravidIndia34410,8891283Inzamam-ul-HaqPakistan37811,7391083Ricky PontingAustralia37513,7043082Virat KohliIndia32215,1955580Mahela JayawardeneSri Lanka44812,6501977MS DhoniIndia35010,7731073Sourav GangulyIndia31111,3632272Root's milestone came in a crucial contest for England, who bounced back emphatically after being bowled out for 132 in the series opener at Perth. His 62-run contribution was part of a strong batting display led by Tom Banton, who struck 121 off 99 balls for his second ODI century.Root and Banton put together a 135-run partnership after England lost Ben Duckett early. Following Root's dismissal, Jordan Cox (67) and Will Jacks (54 not out) added further momentum with a 102-run stand, helping England finish on 355/6.Australia's chase never really recovered from a disastrous start. Gus Atkinson ripped through the top order, taking three of the first four wickets before finishing with figures of 4/28. Matt Renshaw (63) and Cameron Green (64) attempted to revive the innings with a 98-run partnership, but Liam Dawson and Sam Curran struck at regular intervals to keep the hosts under pressure.Australia were eventually bowled out for 220 in 44.3 overs, handing England a comprehensive 135-run victory and levelling the five-match ODI series 1-1 ahead of Wednesday's decider in Hobart.Root acknowledged the importance of the series decider, particularly with the 2027 ODI World Cup approaching.“When you’ve got a World Cup around the corner, knockout games and big games where it really matters to win a series is what you want,” Root said in a post-match TV interview. “So I’m sure both teams will be really excited for the opportunity.
