articles.title: Umpiring howler goes unnoticed! Paul Reiffel, Wayne Knights miss crucial strike-rotation error in India-New Zealand 5th ODI
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: An unusual umpiring error went unnoticed during the fifth ODI between India and New Zealand at Bay Oval in Mount Maunganui on Sunday, with both
articles.body: NEW DELHI: An unusual umpiring error went unnoticed during the fifth ODI between India and New Zealand at Bay Oval in Mount Maunganui on Sunday, with both on-field umpires and the third umpire seemingly missing a mistake involving the strike rotation after a drinks break.The incident occurred at the end of the 14th over of India's innings when Axar Patel took a single off Blair Tickner's bowling. However, when play resumed after the scheduled drinks break, it was Shreyas Iyer who took strike at the beginning of the 15th over instead of Axar.The mix-up went unnoticed by on-field umpires Paul Reiffel and Wayne Knights, while the third umpire also did not intervene to correct the apparent error.According to the ball-by-ball commentary, Axar took the single on the final delivery of the 14th over, which should have put him on strike for the next over. However, Kristian Clarke bowled the first delivery of the 15th over to Iyer, who defended it without scoring.The game continued without the officials addressing the apparent strike-rotation mistake.How the strike-rotation error happenedThe incident unfolded on the final delivery of the 14th over, when Tickner bowled a short delivery to Axar. The Indian all-rounder made room and attempted to guide the ball over the infield, with the ball going over wicketkeeper Tim Seifert and the slip fielder.New Zealand's Duffy ran around from third man to prevent further damage, allowing the Indian batters to complete just one run.The single meant Axar should have faced the first delivery after the drinks interval. Instead, Iyer remained at the striker's end when the teams returned to the field.The first ball of the 15th over was a fullish delivery from Clarke, which Iyer met with a solid forward defence.The error was particularly striking because the drinks interval provided an opportunity for the officials to verify the batting positions before play resumed. However, neither the on-field officials nor the third umpire appeared to notice the discrepancy.India recover after early batting collapseThe unusual incident came during a difficult period for India, who were attempting to rebuild after losing their top-order batters cheaply.The visitors had already suffered early setbacks, with both Axar and Iyer surviving dropped chances before the drinks break. The pitch offered some assistance to the New Zealand bowlers, with occasional bounce and deliveries holding up on the surface.India eventually recovered through contributions from Axar and Ishan Kishan, both of whom scored 46, while Naman Dhir added a late 22 to take the visitors to 209 all out in 42.1 overs.India's bowlers subsequently produced a remarkable comeback, defending the modest target to secure a 22-run victory and seal the five-match ODI series 3-1.Arshdeep Singh led the bowling effort with 3/30 as New Zealand were bowled out for 187 in 48.1 overs.The two sides will next meet in a two-Test series beginning November 19.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Skipper Bryce sets new Scotland run record in win over UAE
articles.summary: Kathyrn and Sarah Bryce shine as Scotland earn a seven-wicket win over host nation United Arab Emirates at the ICC Women's Emerging Nations Trophy.
articles.body:
United Arab Emirates 138-4 (20 overs): Oza 64, Hotchandani 43; Gordon 2-24

Scotland 142-3 (18.1 overs): K Bryce 51, S Bryce 43; Dharnidharka 2-22

Captain Kathyrn Bryce became Scotland Women's all-time leading run scorer as she hit an unbeaten half century to Scotland to a seven-wicket win over host nation United Arab Emirates at the ICC Women's Emerging Nations Trophy.

The skipper hit seven fours on her way to 51 not out as Scotland reached 142-3 with 11 balls to spare.

It takes her international run total to 3562, one more than Kari Carswell.

Her sister, Sarah Bryce, made 43, batting at number three after Darcey Carter's departure in the first over.

Katherine Fraser added 15, with Pippa Sproul on 16 not out.

Batting first, captain Esha Oza led the way with 64 not out as UAE reached 138-4 in their 20 overs.

Heena Hotchandani added 43 before she was one of two batters to be stumped by wicketkeeper Sarah Bryce from the bowling of Kirstie Gordon.

Having previously beaten Papua New Guinea and lost to Sri Lanka, Scotland sit second in Group A and are assured of a place in the Super Six stage.

Scotland conclude their group games against Ireland on Wednesday.

articles.title: ICC finalises global cricket calendar till 2035: India to host 2029 Champions Trophy, co-host 2031 World Cup
articles.summary: The International Cricket Council (ICC) has approved the schedule for its major men's events through 2035 while finalising qualification formats for three
articles.body: The International Cricket Council (ICC) has approved the schedule for its major men's events through 2035 while finalising qualification formats for three global tournaments, including the 2027 Men's ODI World Cup and the 2028 Men's and Women's T20 World Cups.The decisions were taken at the ICC Board meetings in Bali, Indonesia, on Sunday, with the governing body emphasising the need to strengthen qualification pathways and create greater opportunities for both Full and Associate Members.The ICC also confirmed the dates and hosts for the final qualification events for cricket's return to the Olympic programme at the Los Angeles 2028 Games (LA28). The men's Olympic Qualifier will be held in the USA from February 5 to 13, 2028, while the women's event will take place in Bangladesh from February 26 to March 5.ICC CEO Sanjog Gupta said the decisions would provide greater long-term visibility to players and member associations, allowing them to develop structured calendars, high-performance programmes and improved player pathways."The ICC events portfolio and schedule are critical components of cricket's global architecture and deliver elevated context, competitiveness and consequence to the ecosystem," Gupta said.ICC's major men's events calendar until 2035The ICC Board has approved the windows for major men's events from the 2028 Men's T20 World Cup in Australia and New Zealand through to the 2035 Men's Cricket World Cup.The calendar includes four editions of the Men's T20 World Cup, two ODI World Cups, three World Test Championship finals and two Champions Trophy tournaments.The 2029 Men's Champions Trophy will be held in India from October 9 to 28, while India and Bangladesh will jointly host the 2031 Men's Cricket World Cup from October 9 to November 23.England will host the 2029 and 2031 World Test Championship finals, scheduled for June 8-12 and June 12-16, respectively.The 2030 Men's T20 World Cup will be staged in England, Ireland and Scotland from July 4 to August 4. The 2032 and 2034 editions of the tournament are scheduled for October 14 to November 14 and July 6 to August 6, respectively, with hosts yet to be confirmed.The 2033 Champions Trophy will run from October 2 to 23, while the 2033 and 2035 World Test Championship finals are scheduled for June 9-13 and June 7-11, respectively. The host nations for these events are yet to be announced.The 2035 Men's Cricket World Cup, scheduled from October 2 to November 18, will bring the approved calendar to a close.2027 ODI World Cup: 10-team qualifier, four places at stakeThe ICC Men's Cricket World Cup Qualifier 2027, scheduled for February and March 2027, will feature 10 teams competing in 23 matches.The tournament will begin with two groups of five teams each, followed by semi-finals and a final. The top four teams will secure qualification for the 2027 ODI World Cup.However, the qualification process will have an additional layer. The tournament winner will progress directly to the World Cup's Group Stage, while the other three qualified teams will compete in a Super Series to determine the final Group Stage spot.Eight direct qualification spots for 2028 Men's T20 World CupThe 2028 Men's T20 World Cup Global Qualifier will feature 16 teams and 31 matches, with the tournament scheduled to take place in the first quarter of 2028.The teams will be divided into four groups of four, followed by quarter-finals, semi-finals and a final. Eight teams will qualify directly for the 2028 tournament from the Global Qualifier.The ICC has also outlined a regional representation mechanism to ensure geographical diversity in the final line-up. The highest-placed team from each region will qualify, subject to minimum performance criteria, with the remaining places going to the next best-ranked teams overall.The four semi-finalists will automatically advance and will be included in the overall ranking. The four losing quarter-finalists will be ranked from fifth to eighth based on their group-stage position, points, number of wins and net run-rate.Teams finishing third in their respective groups will be ranked from ninth to 12th using the same criteria, while teams finishing fourth will be ineligible for qualification.If a region's highest-ranked team finishes among the semi-finalists or losing quarter-finalists, its representation will already be secured. However, if its highest-ranked team finishes third in a group, it will qualify in place of the lowest-ranked losing quarter-finalist that is not already the highest-placed team from its region.This process will continue until every eligible region is represented, with any remaining qualification places going to the highest-ranked losing quarter-finalists.Women's T20 World Cup 2028: 10 teams already qualifiedThe ICC has also approved the qualification framework for the 2028 Women's T20 World Cup, with 10 teams having already secured their places.Australia, India, South Africa, Bangladesh, England, West Indies, New Zealand, Sri Lanka and Ireland have qualified automatically, alongside hosts Pakistan.The remaining two spots will be decided through a 10-team Global Qualifier.The Netherlands and Scotland, who featured in the 2026 Women's T20 World Cup but did not secure automatic qualification for the 2028 edition, will enter the Global Qualifier directly.They will be joined by eight teams progressing through five regional qualification tournaments scheduled for 2027. The top two teams from the Global Qualifier will complete the 12-team line-up for the 2028 Women's T20 World Cup.LA 2028 Olympic qualificationWith cricket set to return to the Olympic programme at LA28, the ICC has confirmed the hosts and dates for the final qualification tournaments.The men's Olympic Qualifier will be held in Bangladesh from February 5 to 13, 2028, followed by the women's competition in Bangladesh from February 26 to March 5.Both tournaments will feature eight teams divided into two groups of four, with a total of 13 matches in each competition.Teams will play each other once in the group stage, with the two group winners advancing to the final. The winner of each final will secure the last available qualification berth for the respective Olympic competition.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: England beat Australia in second ODI: Sonny Baker new-ball switch from Jofra Archer pays off in Adelaide
articles.summary: Gus Atkinson (4-28) and Sonny Baker (1-45) reduce Australia to 29-4 in devastating opening spell as England bounce back from Perth drubbing to level ODI series with 135-run win in Adelaide; series decider takes place in Hobart on Wednesday (play starts at 3.30am, UK time)
articles.body:
Tom Banton (121 off 99 balls) was rightly named Player of the Match for his second ODI hundred that helped turn things round after a dismal defeat in Perth - from 131 all out to 355-6 in the space of 48 hours - but the bowling was equally impressive.

Gus Atkinson (4-28) claimed career-best ODI figures as he and Sonny Baker (1-45) helped set the tone early on by reducing Australia to 29-4 in the opening seven overs of their run-chase as they were ultimately bowled out for 220.

"The way England's bowlers attacked the first 10 overs, they didn't allow [Mitch] Marsh and [Travis] Head to get away, in terms of giving them any freebies," former England captain Sir Alastair Cook said on TNT Sports .

"They knew they'd come after them - Head hit a brilliant shot for six off a decent ball - but the way Atkinson and Baker bowled, they were made to work for their runs.

"I really liked how Baker got some movement out of the ball, that's his role in the side.

"You've got Archer and Atkinson who will hit the pitch hard - Archer, in this game, serving as the enforcer in the middle overs - so Baker using his swing up front was impressive.

"The [four] wickets early on made such a difference to the game. It was pretty much done early on, unless there was an extraordinary innings from one of the Aussies.

"Full credit to England for the way they adapted and used their bowlers in the right places."

Cook added: "Australia is a really hard place to go 1-0 down in any format. They're great front-runners, so to turn that round like they did after only 48 hours is absolutely superb.

"The leadership group should take a lot of credit for managing to get those players in the right frame of mind after the drubbing they got in Perth."

Baker-Archer switch grants 'England 'two bites at the cherry'

Baker - playing in just his fifth ODI - taking the new ball over Atkinson's usual accomplice, the more experienced Archer, was a bold move but one that paid off for England.

Though Atkinson was the standout, Baker arguably deserved greater reward for his own probing opening spell, in which he dismissed Marsh (2) and had Josh Inglis dropped - Joe Root taking a stunning catch to dismiss the Australian skipper before he was then the guilty party in putting down Inglis.

"Baker's enthusiasm, you can tell he just loves playing cricket for England," former England wicketkeeper Matt Prior added on TNT Sports .

"I'm with Cooky. I'm really pleased that he was given the new ball, where he bowled full and tried to swing it.

"Brook has to take some credit as captain for making that decision."

England have 14 further ODIs scheduled ahead of the start of the 2027 Cricket World Cup in Africa in 11 months' time, and so might the Baker and Archer new-ball switch something they look to run with from here?

"The change in using Jofra Archer through the middle [overs], I like that move," Australia batting consultant Mike Hussey told TNT Sports .

"It gives England two bites at the cherry. They get to attack with Baker and Atkinson at the start and, if things go well, they've got Archer to come in behind that and continue to build pressure.

"Even if things don't go well at the start, it's nice to know you've got someone of world-class quality to come in to arrest some of the momentum."

As for who has the edge going into Wednesday's series decider in Hobart (3.30am UK start time), Hussey fears the worst for Australia.

"England go into the final game with momentum because they've managed to turn things around [from Perth] straight away," he added.

"I think England will certainly take a lot of confidence away from this game. If they take the right attitude again into the final match in Hobart and start well, they'll be on their way towards a series win."

Schedule for England's tour of Australia

ODIs 3.30am UK time, with T20s 8.15am UK time

First ODI (Perth): Australia won seven wickets

Second ODI (Adelaide): England won by 135 runs

Third ODI: Wednesday November 18 (Hobart)

First T20I: Saturday November 21 (Melbourne)

Second T20I: Tuesday November 24 (Carrara)

Third T20I: Friday November 27 (Brisbane)

Fourth T20I: Sunday November 29 (Sydney)

Fifth T20I: Wednesday December 2 (Canberra)

articles.title: 'We did likewise': Mohit Ulva reveals why India celebrated aggressively after beating Pakistan
articles.summary: India U-19 batter Mohit Ulva has explained the emotions behind the team's animated celebrations following their dramatic one-wicket victory over Pakistan
articles.body: India U-19 batter Mohit Ulva has explained the emotions behind the team's animated celebrations following their dramatic one-wicket victory over Pakistan in the Under-19 Asia Cup final, insisting that the players were simply celebrating their triumph and had no intention of provoking their opponents.Mohit, who played a decisive role in India's remarkable chase with an unbeaten 49 off just 26 balls, said the celebrations were a natural reaction to the occasion, given the intensity of an India-Pakistan contest and the fact that it was a final.The celebrations that followed, however, became a talking point, with several Indian players facing criticism on social media for their aggressive gestures towards the Pakistani players.Mohit revealed that the celebrations were a spontaneous expression of the emotions surrounding an India-Pakistan final. He also recalled how the Indian youngsters had not taken Pakistan's celebrations during the league-stage encounter personally."It is natural. It was an India vs Pakistan match, and additionally, a final. The way they celebrated after beating us in the league stage. Actually, we were not even taking their celebration personally. We were thinking that they were celebrating their own victory. It doesn't matter what they do."We did likewise. We were celebrating our own victory. It had emotions, aggression, and everything. We weren't doing it to show them anything. We were celebrating among ourselves, and everything was natural," Mohit told Star Sports.'I couldn't believe I had finished it'India were staring at defeat after slipping to 252/8 in the 42nd over of the chase. However, Mohit and Manal Chauhan refused to give up, putting together a crucial 57-run partnership for the ninth wicket to keep India's hopes alive.Manal scored 47 off 32 balls before departing, leaving India needing 36 more runs with just one wicket remaining. Mohit then received support from No. 11 C Venkata, who remained unbeaten on 11 off eight deliveries.The equation eventually came down to three runs off the final ball, with Mohit finding the boundary to seal the title. Recalling the extraordinary finish, the youngster admitted that he was initially unable to process what had happened."Actually, I was completely zoned out after hitting three runs on one ball with a four. I didn't know that everyone was running to me; everything was happening."It was done; I finished the game. Until it was over, I believed that I would finish it. But after I did it, I couldn't believe that I had finished it. So, I was a little zoned out."After a while, I realised that it was actually over. Everyone was getting up, everyone was celebrating. So, I celebrated a little. I went to the supporters of India, who were sitting there the whole day. I went to them and celebrated with them. It's a very good feeling. Even now, it's a very good feeling for me. Because for my family, for my country, for India, it's a good feeling to win such a match," he added.'No one had any doubt'Mohit also revealed that the Indian dressing room remained confident of pulling off the chase despite losing eight wickets. The young batter credited the encouragement he received from the team's support staff and his conversations with Manal for helping him remain composed during the decisive phase.According to Mohit, the plan was straightforward: one of the two batters needed to stay until the final delivery and take India home."No one had any doubt that we wouldn't be able to do it. Everyone knew that our team had the capability to do it. I was there when we were already 8 wickets down."Sir gave me the confidence that if I play the last ball, I'll do it. Manal was playing; I talked to him. Manal told me to stay till the end. If any one of us plays the last ball, we'll win. Whatever Manal and I planned, whatever we thought, at that moment, it happened. Actually, our execution was on point."We needed a lot of luck in that. Because anything can happen out of the box. We thought that if this plan was going on, they might even bluff in the plan. But they didn't. Everything went on point, as we had planned. At that time, I was very calm. I was feeling good inside. It was a natural moment. It was a natural celebration for me," he added.Mohit's unbeaten knock and Manal's crucial contribution helped India pull off one of their most memorable victories in the tournament, completing a successful chase of 338 to defeat Pakistan by one wicket off the final ball.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘He takes pressure off’: Lakshya Raichandani on Aaryavir Sehwag’s impact in India’s Asia Cup triumph
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India Under-19 captain Lakshya Raichandani has credited Aaryavir Sehwag’s attacking batting for making life easier for his teammates, saying
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India Under-19 captain Lakshya Raichandani has credited Aaryavir Sehwag’s attacking batting for making life easier for his teammates, saying the opener’s ability to put opposition bowlers under pressure takes the burden off the batter at the other end.Aaryavir was one of the standout performers in India's Under-19 Asia Cup title-winning campaign, finishing as the tournament's leading run-scorer with 361 runs in five innings. His consistent performances also earned him the player-of-the-tournament award.Praising the opener's contribution, Raichandani described him as both a fine batter and a wonderful human being, while explaining how his approach changes the dynamics of an innings."Yeah, he's a really good batter (Aaryavir) and a wonderful human being. When he bats, it takes some pressure off the batter at the other end because of the way he plays. It also makes batting easier on the track, as he puts the opposition bowlers under pressure and forces them to release that pressure by offering loose deliveries to the other batter," Raichandani said.‘We never stopped believing’: India bounce back against PakistanIndia's triumph was particularly special as they overcame a group-stage defeat to arch-rivals Pakistan before beating them by one wicket in a nail-biting final in Al Amerat, Oman, on Saturday.Reflecting on his experience of leading the side to the title, Raichandani said the team developed a strong understanding throughout the campaign."It was a pretty good experience. We had a really good rapport with each other, and it was a great experience overall. I'm proud of the guys and really privileged to be leading this team," he said.The captain also explained the team's straightforward batting approach, stressing the importance of making the most of the powerplay and having at least one set batter stay until the end."My approach was simple. If one batter gets set at one end and takes the innings deep, it makes the chase much easier. Our approach was straightforward, and getting a good start in the powerplay was important."Hopefully, we managed to provide that start, and the plan after that was for one of the set batters to stay till the end," the skipper said.Raichandani admitted the group-stage loss to Pakistan provided important lessons, but insisted that the team's belief in its approach never wavered."In the first match, our plan was quite simple. After losing, we realised the areas where we could improve and where we could have done better. That was one important takeaway. Overall, though, our plan remained the same, and we believed in our approach," he said."We never stopped believing. We were quite optimistic, and we continued to believe in the team till the very end."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Yash Thakur joins Sachin Tendulkar, MS Dhoni in unwanted list after ODI debut against New Zealand
articles.summary: India pacer Yash Thakur endured a forgettable start to his ODI career after being dismissed for a duck on debut in the fifth and final match against New
articles.body: India pacer Yash Thakur endured a forgettable start to his ODI career after being dismissed for a duck on debut in the fifth and final match against New Zealand at Bay Oval on Sunday. In doing so, the right-arm pacer joined an unwanted list of Indian cricketers that includes batting legends Sachin Tendulkar and MS Dhoni.Thakur became the 18th Indian batter to register a duck on ODI debut, with his name joining some prominent players who experienced a similar fate in their first appearance in the format.The list dates back to 1974, when former India captain Bishan Singh Bedi was dismissed without scoring on his ODI debut. Sachin Tendulkar, who made his first ODI appearance in 1989, and Dhoni, who began his international career in the format in 2004, also featured on the list.Other notable names include VVS Laxman, Suresh Raina, Shikhar Dhawan and former India all-rounder Roger Binny.Indian players dismissed for a duck on ODI debutYearPlayer1974Bishan Singh Bedi1979Surinder Khanna1980Roger Binny1980Yograj Singh1981K Srikkanth1984Ashok Patel1985Lalchand Rajput1988Sanjeev Sharma1989Sachin Tendulkar1998VVS Laxman1999Gyanendra Pandey2002Jai Prakash Yadav2003Avishkar Salvi2004MS Dhoni2005Suresh Raina2006Wasim Jaffer2010Shikhar Dhawan2026Yash ThakurThakur's debut came in a series-deciding contest, with India looking to bounce back after their humiliating 244-run defeat in the fourth ODI, where they were bowled out for just 89.The fifth ODI, however, turned out to be another challenging outing with the bat for the visitors. Asked to bat first, India lost Rohit Sharma early before Virat Kohli and Ruturaj Gaikwad also departed, leaving the team struggling at 34/3.Shreyas Iyer and Axar Patel attempted to steady the innings with a 52-run partnership for the fourth wicket, but New Zealand kept chipping away at regular intervals. Axar and Ishan Kishan scored 46 apiece, while Naman Dhir contributed 22.India were eventually bowled out for 209 in 42.1 overs, with Mitchell Santner and Jacob Duffy claiming three wickets each.However, the Indian bowlers made up for the batting disappointment. Mohammad Siraj and Arshdeep Singh struck early to put New Zealand under pressure, with Arshdeep eventually finishing with 3/30 and Siraj taking 2/50.Thakur also made an early contribution with the ball, taking the catch to dismiss New Zealand opener Tim Seifert off Siraj's bowling. New Zealand were eventually dismissed for 187 in 48.1 overs, handing India a 22-run victory.The win secured a 3-1 series triumph for India and ended New Zealand's run of 11 consecutive ODI series victories at home. It also completed a successful white-ball leg of the tour for the visitors, who had earlier won the five-match T20I series 3-2.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Record alert! Kagiso Rabada surpasses Allan Donald in South Africa’s all-time wicket tally
articles.summary: Kagiso Rabada added another milestone to his illustrious career on Sunday, surpassing legendary fast bowler Allan Donald to become South Africa’s
articles.body: Kagiso Rabada added another milestone to his illustrious career on Sunday, surpassing legendary fast bowler Allan Donald to become South Africa’s fourth-highest wicket-taker in international cricket. However, the landmark moment was followed by a spirited Bangladesh fightback on the opening day of the first Test.Rabada claimed five wickets for 51 runs to take his international tally across Tests, ODIs and T20Is to 606, moving past Donald's 602. Shaun Pollock leads the South African charts with 823 wickets, followed by Dale Steyn (697) and Makhaya Ntini (661).The 31-year-old also registered his 18th five-wicket haul in Test cricket, drawing level with Ntini for joint-third place on South Africa's all-time list. Donald is second with 20 five-fors, while Steyn leads the standings with 26.Rabada strikes early as Bangladesh lose top orderRabada made an immediate impact, striking twice in the opening exchanges as Bangladesh endured a difficult start. Debutant Mahfijul Islam fell for a first-ball duck, while Mominul Haque also departed without scoring.The fast bowler then produced a superb delivery to dismiss Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain Shanto, leaving the visitors reeling at 22/3.Tanzid Hasan and Towhid Hridoy attempted to stabilise the innings with a valuable partnership. Tanzid scored 67 before Rabada returned after lunch to remove him and Mushfiqur Rahim in quick succession, completing his five-wicket haul.Bangladesh were struggling at 121/5, but the contest took a dramatic turn thereafter.Hridoy, Litton script remarkable recoveryHridoy found an able partner in Litton Das as the duo turned the innings around with an unbroken sixth-wicket stand of 206 runs, the highest partnership by a Bangladesh pair against South Africa in their Test encounters.Hridoy produced a magnificent 137 off 208 deliveries, registering his maiden Test century against South Africa. He became only the second Bangladesh batter to score a Test hundred against the Proteas after Mahmudul Hasan Joy in 2022.Litton, meanwhile, remained unbeaten on 92 as Bangladesh finished the opening day at 327/6, recovering from a precarious position to take control of the innings.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Chadd Sayers: Former Australian bowler rejects Pat Cummins' claims about 'Sandpapergate': 'Everyone knew what was going on'
articles.summary: Chadd Sayers, a former Australia bowler, disagreed with Pat Cummins' account of the ball tampering plot known as Sandpapergate; Sayers insisted that "everyone in that side knew what was going on and what was being used"
articles.body:
Sayers, who was 12th man in the ill-fated Newlands Test and won his only cap in the subsequent match, has lined up alongside Khawaja, having previously claimed "everything Usman said was accurate".

Speaking to SEN Radio ahead of the second ODI against England in Adelaide, the 39-year-old said: "I'm comfortable sitting here right now and where I stand on the situation, that I believe everyone in that side knew what was going on and what was being used.

"It [sandpaper] was used in two Test matches and there were discussions in change-rooms of how we were going to get the ball to reverse and what was going to be used.

"My recollection isn't as clear as it was obviously eight years ago, I just know that there were numerous conversations of it around in the change-rooms. I knew that it was going to be used, as I believe everyone else did."

Sayers also revealed his own role, which involved taking the offending item off the field when he was performing his 12th man duties.

"The plan was that Cameron Bancroft was going to take that out, the ball was going to be dropped on the ground by the umpires, and he was going to go about business," he said.

"[The sandpaper] was given to me to take off. I was just the player who took the drinks out at the time. [I came] on to the field with drinks and, yeah, it was passed on to me.

"I was trying to fit into the Australian side, probably similar to Cam Bancroft, and we were probably a young demographic then. We didn't know how big it was going to get and I guess you probably don't think you're going to get caught doing it."

Sayers stated the issue of who would publicly accept responsibility was discussed by the team for between 60 and 90 minutes - another detail Cummins has denied being part of.

Reflecting on his admissions, the 39-year-old added: "It's been hard because you obviously got to tiptoe around and not be able to tell the truth.

"It's probably a relief now that it's out there in the open and now you can speak openly about it. It's a bit of a relief that it's out."
